title: Desolace
body: Desolace is a grey and broken land southwest of the Stonetalon Mountains, a waste of bare rock, bleached bones and brackish yellow pools beneath a stormy sky. Only the western shore, where the Veiled Sea breaks on the Sar'theris Strand, keeps any green. This is the ancestral home of the centaur. The Cenarion Circle says the race was born long ago of Zaetar, first son of Cenarius, and the earth elemental Theradras, and that the children repaid their father by killing him. Their clans, the Kolkar, Gelkis, Magram and Maraudine, now fight one another across the plains, and outsiders dread the day they might unite. They are not the only danger. The night elves who once lived here are long gone, the Burning Blade holds Thunder Axe Fortress, demons gather at Mannoroc Coven, Hatefury satyrs haunt Sargeron and naga prowl the coast. The Alliance keeps watch from Nijel's Point in the northern mountains, while the Horde holds Ghost Walker Post above the Kodo Graveyard and the troll fishing village of Shadowprey.

title: Nijel's Point
body: Hidden in the mountains of northern Desolace, just east of the way in from Stonetalon, Nijel's Point is a small Alliance camp, easily missed. No one there seems to know who Nijel was. Soldiers of Stormwind guard it under Captain Pentigast, who studies how to break the warring centaur clans, while Corporal Melkins pays for every centaur ear brought in. Night elves keep the inn and the hippogryph roost, and Vahlarriel Demonslayer has come from Darnassus to find two missing nobles. Kreldig Ungor of Reclaimers Inc. hunts down lost property for paying clients, Brother Anton preaches the cause of the Scarlet Crusade, and the keeper Marandis and his sisters of the Cenarion Circle have business with Maraudon.

title: Sargeron
body: In the northeastern corner of Desolace stand the ruins of a night elf city that has lain broken since the War of the Ancients, its true name forgotten. The Hatefury satyrs who infest it call it Sargeron, after their dark master Sargeras. Rogues, tricksters, betrayers, felsworn, hellcallers and shadowstalkers prowl the fallen streets as allies of the Burning Blade. Maurin Bonesplitter of Ghost Walker Post wants a shadowstalker's scalp to break a demon lord's wards against scrying. Kreldig Ungor of Nijel's Point doubts the tale that the satyr are tied to the night elves, blaming it on the one elf who brought them into the war a few years back.

title: Thunder Axe Fortress
body: Thunder Axe Fortress rises in northern Desolace, just south of the ruins of Tethris Aran, and belongs to the Burning Blade, orcs who have given their loyalty to demons. From its stronghold, barracks and watchtowers the cult's augurs, adepts, reavers, felsworn and shadowmages practice their dark craft. Within lies a red crystal sealing the Demon Box, which holds the Hand of Iruxos the cult uses to open portals at Mannoroc Coven, and atop one watchtower a Burning Blade seer studies the Sceptre of Light, taken from the naga. When the Darnassian nobles Dalinda and Tyranis Malem were seized on the road, the cultists dragged them here, and Dalinda feared she would be sacrificed to their demon masters.

title: Ethel Rethor
body: On the northwestern coast the ruins of Ethel Rethor lie mostly beneath the waves, a drowned night elf city whose only standing remnant is a lone tower reached by a small bridge. From it the Argent Dawn mage Azore Aldamort watches both the Slitherblade naga who haunt the shallows and the Burning Blade to the east. Nearby lies the chest of the Stormwind mage Karnitol, who abandoned it when sea giants fell upon his ship offshore and teleported himself and his servants to safety. It was found curiously free of water damage, forced open and empty, its magical wards spent and its sides raked by long, deep gouges that no sword or dagger had made.

title: Ranazjar Isle
body: On Ranazjar Isle, a small rocky island off the northwestern coast, Slitherblade sea witches, tidehunters, myrmidons and oracles gather about a great serpent statue. Close by, sunken night elf ruins on the sea floor serve the Slitherblade as a home. The Argent Dawn knows that a gem set in the statue's hand will call forth Lord Kragaru, protector of the Book of the Ancients, which holds secrets the naga have kept for centuries. Drulzegar Skraghook's fishing crew was slaughtered by naga near the isle, and when Rackmore's ship was attacked by sea creatures on its way to Feathermoon Stronghold, he hid his treasure here in a chest that needs two keys, one silver and one gold.

title: Sar'theris Strand
body: The Sar'theris Strand runs along the western coast, the one stretch of Desolace that still knows sun and grass. Slitherblade naga come ashore from their reefs, drysnap crawlers scuttle in the surf, and Deepstrider giants wade the shallows, the kind of sea giants that drove a Stormwind mage from his ship off the northern shore. A wrecked ship lies off the coast north of Shadowprey Village, where soft-shelled clams prized by troll fishermen as bait litter the sea bed, and waterlogged footlockers turn up among the rocks. Near Shadowprey, the dryad Selendra and her sisters have come down from Stonetalon on a mission they cannot finish alone, and seek mortals strong enough to help.

title: Kormek's Hut
body: Kormek's Hut is a lonely shack on the barren flats of north-central Desolace, southeast of Thunder Axe Fortress, and of Kormek himself there is no sign. The goblin Bibbly F'utzbuckle has taken over its pen, sure that he is sitting on a goldmine. Kodo bones from the graveyard to the south, he claims, go into furniture, musical instruments and even blasting powder, and a caravan collects them to sell at Shadowprey Village. That caravan, the Gizelton brothers' kodo train, halts on the road outside. Inside waits a stranger guest, Willow of the Twilight's Hammer, who pays for crystal carvings from the caverns of Maraudon, relics of the old gods whose powers, Willow says, have been too long at rest.

title: Kolkar Village
body: The Kolkar hold the eastern reaches of Desolace from a village northeast of Ghost Walker Post, beneath the mountains. Desolace is their homeland, and from it their warbands have spread into the Barrens. The Horde holds that as long as the clan stays strong here it will always be a threat. Battle lords, destroyers, maulers, windchasers and scouts crowd the camp under Khan Dez'hepah. The rival clans scorn them: the Gelkis say the Kolkar would not know true magic if it bit them, and the Magram laugh as they kill them. Travelers fear them all the same. When the Gizelton caravan hears the Kolkar war drums, it stops dead on the road and waits for a bodyguard.

title: Scrabblescrew's Camp
body: Smeed Scrabblescrew's camp sits beside the road through central Desolace, a goblin's stake in the only caravan brave enough to cross these lands. Smeed claims to have learned how to rejuvenate and control aged and dying kodo with a device of his own, the kodo kombobulator, which jolts the beasts into tame pack animals. He supplies them to Cork and Rigger Gizelton, whose caravan pays his bills, and he pays the bodyguards who see it safely through, though he grumbles at every coin. Smeed fancies himself a far better businessman than Bibbly F'utzbuckle of Kormek's Hut, and can hardly wait to see the look on his rival's green face when word of his success gets around.

title: Ghost Walker Post
body: Ghost Walker Post is a tauren outpost in central Desolace, north of the great Kodo Graveyard, reached by the road south from the Charred Vale. From here the Horde deals with the centaur clans and the Burning Blade. The tauren Gurda Wildmane seeks an alliance with one of the clans, while Felgur Twocuts gathers intelligence on them. Orgrimmar sent its own envoys, the orc swordsman Takata Steelblade and the Forsaken warlock Maurin Bonesplitter, to root out the demons, at the word of Keldran. Ghost Walker braves keep watch, Nataka Longhorn longs for fried fish from Shadowprey, and Narv Hidecrafter swears the strongest hides come from kodo that have laid themselves to rest in this wasteland.

title: Kodo Graveyard
body: South of Ghost Walker Post spreads the Kodo Graveyard, a field of enormous skeletons where kodo come to lay themselves to rest. Aged, dying and ancient kodo wander slowly among the bones of their kin, and carrion horrors haunt the field. Many of the bones seem to have belonged to beasts far larger than any kodo alive today, and grave moss grows thick in their shadow. Where death gathers, so do goblins. Bibbly F'utzbuckle of Kormek's Hut pays for every bone carried out of here, and Hornizz Brimbuzzle keeps a camp at the graveyard's edge, forever waiting on his restless sister Melizza and the next deal, even one made of ghosts.

title: Mannoroc Coven
body: Named for the pit lord Mannoroth, Mannoroc Coven lies south of Ghost Walker Post among old night elf ruins, a land already dead that the demons have blasted further with fel magic. Burning Blade summoners opened portals here, and through them the Legion came: lesser infernals, doomwarders, felhounds that hunt mages, and succubi called nether maidens, sisters and sorceresses. Their master is the demon lord Azrethoc, whose signature marks a contract carried by the cult, and the orc warlock Jugkar Grim'rod serves at his side. Even the Gizelton caravan's kodo shy at the coven. At its southern edge an exiled centaur, the Pariah, nurses his dream of a single great tribe.

title: Shadowbreak Ravine
body: Hidden in the mountains southeast of Magram Village, Shadowbreak Ravine is a secret enclave of the Burning Blade, far from the eyes of travelers on the road. Summoners and invokers of the cult practice their arts here, kin to those who call demons into Mannoroc Coven, and ley hunters, felhounds that feed on magic, prowl among them. The cultists keep something else in the ravine as well: captured stallions, kept beside dark steeds that bear the cult's name, the Burning Blade nightmares. What the cultists mean to do with them they do not say.

title: Magram Village
body: The Magram centaur hold the southeast of Desolace, their camps spread out at the foot of the eastern mountains. They are a clan that respects only strength. Wranglers, stormers, marauders, maulers and windchasers run with their bonepaws, and sacks of dried meat are stored so the clan can fight longer between hunts. Khan Jehn rules them, strong, his enemies say, but too sure of his own might. On the outskirts, under the eyes of his bodyguards, waits Warug, the clan's spokesman, who will hear any outsider strong enough to slay the Gelkis. To the Magram, the Gelkis faith in their mother Theradras is nothing but weakness, and they mean to prove it.

title: Valley of Bones
body: At the southern edge of Desolace lies the Valley of Bones, a crag where the vast skeletons of two Dead Goliaths have collapsed against the cliffs, their origin unknown. Undead ravagers stalk its floor, outcast necromancers move among them, and the valley is haunted by the ghosts of the Magram. It draws outsiders all the same. Brother Anton of the Scarlet Crusade sends would-be recruits here to destroy the ravagers as proof of their resolve, and the goblin Hornizz Brimbuzzle hands out crates of ghost magnets to lure the spirits between the two great skeletons, sure that the Magram will pay a fortune for captured ghost-o-plasm, if only he can convince them what it is.

title: Gelkis Village
body: The Gelkis centaur dwell in the far southwest of Desolace, their village ringing a ravine crossed by bridges beside the main road south. Theirs is the clan of the earth. Their shamans call on Theradras, whom they hold to be the mother of the centaur, and trust that she protects them. In the cave of Bolgan's Hole, where Khan Shaka keeps his seat, they hoard the blue crystals called tears of Theradras. The shaman Uthek the Wise waits in a tent on the outskirts for strangers willing to spill Magram blood. The Gelkis and the Magram are brother clans and mortal enemies, set apart by faith in the earth against faith in strength.

title: Valley of Spears
body: The Valley of Spears in western Desolace belongs to the Maraudine, the clan that guards Maraudon, holy ground where only spirits and the most sacred priests may tread. Maraudine scouts, stormers and priests roam its canyons, and ghostly raiders ride among them. A war horn stands atop a high bluff, and its call brings the clan's warriors and at last Khan Hratha himself. In the caves at the valley's end the dryad Cavindra begs for help for her cursed brother and sisters, and the Nameless Prophet, one of the oldest of all the tribes, communes with the spirits of the ancestors. The goblin Melizza Brimbuzzle came here to trade and ended up in a cage.

title: Shadowprey Village
body: Shadowprey Village is a Darkspear troll fishing village on the western coast of Desolace, its docks reaching into the sea, and its catch is wanted inland at Ghost Walker Post. Tauren keep the inn and the wind riders. Fishermen of every temper work the docks: Jinar'Zillen pays others to empty his shellfish traps, Mai'Lahii would rather fish than sell tackle, and Drulzegar Skraghook lives only for revenge on the naga who killed his crew. Taiga Wisemane fights the demons of Mannoroc Coven, Vark Battlescar works to heal the corruption of Maraudon, and the tauren Roon Wildmane remembers the days he hunted with the dwarf Hemet Nesingwary. Rokaro, Champion of the Horde, keeps a secret left in his care by Rexxar.

title: Warug
body: Warug speaks for the Magram clan, on the edge of Magram Village, his bodyguards close at hand. He respects strength and nothing else, and will not speak with anyone who has not slain many Gelkis. For those who have, he has work: smash the tears of Theradras the Gelkis hoard, bring him the head of Khan Shaka so he can stare at it and laugh, and break the Maraudine. He laughs when he kills, so the enemy can see he is weak. Yet Warug has a childish streak. Long ago he killed a gnome who came with a cart of strange moving things, and he still wants a new wooden target dummy to replace the one he broke.

title: Uthek the Wise
body: Uthek the Wise is a shaman of the Gelkis who keeps a tent on the outskirts of their village and listens to what the earth tells her. To strangers whose hands are wet with Magram blood she gives tasks and counsel: the Magram hoard meat to fight longer, the Kolkar know nothing of true magic, and the earth has whispered to her of a red crystal called draenethyst, new to this world, from a place where mountains fly and demons rule. She sent one ally as far as the Swamp of Sorrows for a shard of it. Earth magic, Uthek says, is stronger than any khan's might, and one day the Gelkis will rule.

title: Captain Pentigast
body: Captain Pentigast commands the Stormwind soldiers who guard Nijel's Point. He sees Desolace as a land at war, and fears that whichever centaur clan wins will spill out and threaten the Alliance's strongholds. His answer is cold reckoning. The clans fight among themselves, and if they ever joined into one force they would be unstoppable, so the Alliance must press its advantage: side with the Gelkis or the Magram, earn their favor by killing their rivals, and learn from them how to beat all the centaurs. His corporal, Melkins, holds to a simpler policy, paying for centaur ears in the belief that each one brings the war a step closer to its end.

title: Takata Steelblade
body: Takata Steelblade is an orc swordsman of Orgrimmar who stands watch at Ghost Walker Post against the demons of Desolace, beside the warlock Maurin Bonesplitter. When Maurin's scrying revealed the demon lord Azrethoc, Takata judged that even the creature's image held more power than his companion, and he would have gone to face it himself, yet he would not shame his clan by abandoning his duties for his own glory. Instead he trusted others to strike at Mannoroc Coven. The demons only seem to multiply, and at times he wishes the centaur were his only foes, but he holds to the hope that the Horde may one day have a place it can safely call home again.

title: Maurin Bonesplitter
body: Maurin Bonesplitter is a Forsaken warlock at Ghost Walker Post who knows the ways of the Burning Blade and holds them in contempt: their magic is feeble, he says, and what power they have is borrowed from the masters they serve. He can read a demon's contract written in runes only distantly related to Eredun, and he works with care, for a wrong reagent could kill the one who scries, and fate, he admits, has dealt him pain enough. Hunting the demon lord Azrethoc would win favor with the Warchief, favor he means to turn to his own ends, and he steers the proud Takata Steelblade with a light hand, so the swordsman believes the plan his own.

title: Tyranis Malem
body: Tyranis Malem is a son of House Malem, a Darnassian merchant family, who came to Desolace with his sister Dalinda despite every warning about its demons. He had lately begun to crave knowledge of all things arcane, against the wishes of his people, and Darnassus already had doubts about his motives. When the Burning Blade slaughtered the siblings' guards and dragged them to Thunder Axe Fortress, Tyranis tried to impress his captors with his learning. His sister feared he would seek the cult's secrets and count himself among them. She was right. He is found among the cultists, an elf given over to the very powers his people most dread.

title: Azore Aldamort
body: Azore Aldamort is a human mage of the Argent Dawn who keeps the lone tower of Ethel Rethor on the northwestern coast, with two threats in view. The Burning Blade of Thunder Axe Fortress is rumored to have taken the Sceptre of Light from the naga, an artifact said in legend to sink whole cities beneath the sea, and a seer of the cult studies it from a watchtower. The Slitherblade naga, meanwhile, guard secrets kept for centuries in the Book of the Ancients, watched by a guardian on Ranazjar Isle. To trusted allies Azore entrusts the Gem of the Serpent to call that guardian out, meaning to pass the book on to the high council.

title: Brother Anton
body: Brother Anton is an emissary of the Scarlet Crusade. Hearing rumors of an undead infestation in distant Desolace, he booked passage to Kalimdor at once to seek out and destroy it, and now preaches at Nijel's Point. His creed is war with the Scourge, an evil that corrupts the people and infects the land. Those who would join must first prove themselves against the undead ravagers of the Valley of Bones. The worthy he sends back across the sea with a letter of commendation for Raleigh the Devout in Southshore, who will escort them to the Crusade's Scarlet Monastery, for the true threat of the plague, he insists, lies in Lordaeron.

title: The Centaur Pariah
body: At the southern edge of Mannoroc Coven lives a centaur exiled as a heretic, known only as the Pariah. He believes the tribes have forgotten themselves, fighting one another for scraps left by vultures and lands infested by the Legion, when their heritage is as noble as any night elf's or orc's. His dream is one great tribe. The Nameless Prophet within Maraudon, he says, wears the Amulet of Spirits without knowing its power, and its five missing gems are held by the ghosts of the first khans, Kolk, Gelk, Magra, Maraudos and Veng. Made whole as the Amulet of Union, it would give him the strength to reunite the clans. No centaur could help him without damnation.

title: The Kolkar of Desolace
body: Desolace is a land torn by war, and the Horde means to have its say. From his bunkers in the Barrens, Regthar Deathgate recruits agents for a mission against the centaur, for as long as the Kolkar stay strong in their homeland they will threaten the plains. His volunteers go to Felgur Twocuts at Ghost Walker Post, who has been gathering intelligence on the clans and warns that the struggle will be long. Many clans wander the dry plains, fighting and dying against each other, and that is a mercy, for united they would be a fierce foe. The Horde must act before they unite. First the Kolkar leader, Khan Dez'hepah, must die in his village to the northeast, since strength is what centaur understand best. Then the hunt for ears begins, from any clan at all, until every centaur knows the banner of the Horde. Beyond that, Gurda Wildmane has a subtler plan: ally with one clan and learn from it how to defeat them all.

title: The War of the Clans
body: Captain Pentigast at Nijel's Point and Gurda Wildmane at Ghost Walker Post reach the same conclusion: the way to beat the centaur is through their hatred of one another. An outsider who slays enough Magram may win a hearing with Uthek the Wise of the Gelkis, while one who slays Gelkis may stand before Warug of the Magram. Each clan then demands proof. The Gelkis want the Magram meat stores raided, a draenethyst shard fetched from a far swamp and the head of the Magram Khan Jehn. The Magram want the Gelkis tears of Theradras broken, a new target dummy for Warug's amusement and the head of Khan Shaka. Alliance champions must bloody the Kolkar too. Both roads end in the Valley of Spears, where a war horn atop a high bluff summons the Maraudine until Khan Hratha himself rides out to die, carrying a piece of a key. Each clan swears it will now rule Desolace.

title: Vahlarriel's Search
body: House Malem, a Darnassian merchant family, sent Vahlarriel Demonslayer to Nijel's Point when two of its children, Dalinda and Tyranis, vanished after passing through the Stonetalon Mountains. Their wagon was found wrecked by spells and weapons in a fight that had been swift and one-sided, with no blood and no bodies. A pendant lay in the wreckage, and tracks led south toward a fortress where a fire was kept: Thunder Axe, stronghold of the Burning Blade. Vahlarriel's superiors cared most that Dalinda come home safe; Tyranis was to be gauged first. Dalinda was found a prisoner, and she would not leave until her brother's fate was known. It was the one she dreaded. Tyranis had joined the cult, and he died at her rescuers' hands, as he surely would have at her own people's. Only then did she flee, making her way back to Nijel's Point on her own, to carry her brother's shame home to Darnassus.

title: The Corrupter
body: Among the Burning Blade's cultists some carry a strip of flayed demon skin, rotten-smelling and strangely supple, written over in red. Maurin Bonesplitter at Ghost Walker Post reads it as a contract in an old tongue only distantly like Eredun, signed by a demon: Lord Azrethoc. To find him Maurin needs the scalp of a Hatefury shadowstalker from Sargeron, to break the demon's wards against scrying, and an oracle crystal from the Slitherblade naga of the coast to focus the spell. When he calls Azrethoc by his true name, the demon lord's image appears, and even as an apparition it seems more powerful than Maurin himself. Finding the demon far more dangerous than he expected, Maurin sends word to Takata Steelblade, hoping the swordsman will think the hunt his own idea. Takata agrees that a demon seeking sway over the Burning Blade must be stopped. Azrethoc and his orc warlock servant Jugkar Grim'rod are slain at Mannoroc Coven, and Takata dares to hope the Horde may one day have a place it can safely call home again.

title: The Hand of Iruxos
body: Taiga Wisemane of Shadowprey Village learned that the Burning Blade possesses a Demon Box holding the Hand of Iruxos, the relic the cult uses to open demonic portals at Mannoroc Coven and let a tide of demons into the world. The box lay sealed within a red crystal at Thunder Axe Fortress, and Taiga provided a demon pick to break it free, though a demon spirit rose to guard it. Back at Shadowprey the box was opened, revealing the gruesome Hand. Then Taiga turned the cult's own tool against it. Carried into Mannoroc Coven, the Hand could banish the portals, though each one sent forth a guardian when touched. With six portals closed the flood of demons was stemmed, and all of Azeroth, Taiga declared, was safer for it.

title: The Karnitol Shipwreck
body: Reclaimers Inc., the Ironforge firm that finds what people have lost for the right price, sent the dwarf Kreldig Ungor to Nijel's Point with a list of jobs. The first was for Karnitol, a mage and noble of Stormwind, whose ship was attacked by sea giants off the northwest coast. He had tried to bring a valuable chest ashore, then abandoned it and teleported away. The chest was found burned where its magical traps had fired, forced open and empty, scored by long gouges that no blade had made. Kreldig blamed the Slitherblade naga, and Karnitol's satchel turned up among their tidehunters and sea witches. The other job was a shopping list for Leftwitch, a gnome mage of Kharanos: Hatefury horns and claws, scorpashi venom, aged kodo hide and at last felhound brains, nether wings and doomwarder blood from Mannoroc Coven. Kreldig had not even known there were demons in Desolace.

title: The Gizelton Caravan
body: The goblin brothers Cork and Rigger Gizelton run the only caravan brave enough to cross Desolace, a kodo train hauling their wares between a stop outside Kormek's Hut in the north and another on the southern road east of Shadowprey Village. At each stop a selling machine opens for business, Cork's Vendor-Tron 1000 and Rigger's Super-Seller 680, and Cork, his brother says, is sure his own will sell more. The road between is perilous. Near the Kolkar village the centaur war drums make the brothers halt until someone will guard them past, and farther south, where the demons of Mannoroc Coven usually ignore them, something has spooked the kodo. Bodyguards who see them through are paid by their partner Smeed Scrabblescrew, who supplies the kodo and grumbles at the cost, since the brothers clear a single gold piece a week.

title: The Corruption of Maraudon
body: At the end of the Valley of Spears lies Maraudon, holy ground of the centaur and the root of their story. The Cenarion Circle tells it plainly. Ages ago Zaetar, first son of Cenarius and brother of Remulos, came to the earth elemental Princess Theradras, a power somehow kin to the Old Gods, and their offspring became the centaur. The children killed their father, and Theradras keeps his remains in Maraudon still. Keeper Marandis at Nijel's Point and Selendra near Shadowprey have come from Stonetalon to recover them, and seek allies strong enough to slay Theradras. The caverns are fouled besides. The satyr Lord Vyletongue has poisoned them and created Noxxion as a living symbol of his corruption, and Talendria of Nijel's Point and Vark Battlescar of Shadowprey seek to heal the vines he twisted. Outside, Cavindra pleads for her brother Celebras, who wanders the depths cursed, his scepter stolen in two pieces.
